messages:
mika: Quick q — trying to script creds rotation for the CLI. Can we store multiple profiles and rotate keys without any interactive prompts? I'm on redwood-cli v0.9.2 running in GitLab CI.

alex: Yep. The CLI supports named profiles in the config file and also a non-interactive import path. What CI runner are you using for secret storage (Vault, KMS, env vars)?

mika: GitLab with masked variables, but we'd prefer encrypted files because we need to rotate frequently and keep an audit trail.

jamie: Two patterns that worked for us: 1) keep an encrypted token blob in repo (KMS/GCP/AWS) and decrypt during CI, then call the CLI import. 2) use ephemeral service tokens stored in Vault and inject via env var. Both avoid interactive prompts.

mika: Example of (1) would be super helpful — especially the exact CLI commands to import a profile non-interactively.

alex: For non-interactive import we use the --token-file flag. Example:

```bash
# decrypt the token in CI
gcloud kms decrypt --ciphertext-file=release-bot.token.enc --plaintext-file=/tmp/release-bot.token \ 
  --location=global --keyring=ci-keys --key=release-bot-key

# import into a named profile
redwood auth import --profile=release-bot --token-file=/tmp/release-bot.token --no-interactive

# verify profile
redwood config get profile=release-bot
```

jamie: Add `--no-interactive` (as alex shows) to ensure it never prompts. Also `redwood auth import` will create the profile section in ~/.redwood/config by default. If you want to target a specific config file, use `REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH=/ci/home/.redwood/config` in the env.

mika: Ooh — didn't know about REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH. That helps when you want to keep CI isolated. Any gotchas around file permissions?

sam: Make sure the decrypted token file is mode 600 and removed immediately after import. Example in bash: `chmod 600 /tmp/release-bot.token && redwood auth import ... && shred -u /tmp/release-bot.token`. Also avoid logging the token in CI logs.

mika: Good call. How about rotating tokens smoothly without downtime? We run a periodic deploy that reads the profile. Need a safe swap approach.

alex: We do a two-step rotate: create new profile name `release-bot-v2`, import new token there, then switch the active profile atomically via `redwood config set profile=release-bot-v2`. For apps that read env, you can update REDWOOD_PROFILE env var in the deployment system and roll pods. That lets you fallback to old profile name if something breaks.

jamie: For zero-downtime, also stage the new profile in a canary subset of hosts first. If the CLI is embedded in scripts, prefer `redwood auth select --profile=...` (it updates the config file) over editing tokens in-place.

mika: Is there a way for the CLI to read token from stdin so we can keep things entirely in memory in CI?

alex: There's `--token-file /dev/stdin` in unix, but quieter is `redwood auth import --profile=release-bot --token-file=-` which reads from stdin (supported since v0.9.0). Example:

```bash
printf "%s" "$CI_RELEASE_BOT_TOKEN" | redwood auth import --profile=release-bot --token-file=- --no-interactive
```

mika: Perfect. That avoids temp files entirely. We'll use that model.

devex-bot: FYI docs on CLI auth were updated yesterday: https://docs.redwood.ai/cli/auth (section: non-interactive import & config envs) :books:

mika: Thanks all — plan: implement `rotate.sh` in CI that decrypts or reads vault, pipes token into import with --no-interactive, sets REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH to CI-specific file, and atomically flips the profile name used by our deploy. I'll post the script after a test run.

sam: Happy to review the script when you post it. Also add a short note in runbooks about `shred -u` not being available on some alpine images — use `srm` or `rm` as fallback.

mika: Noted. Will post demo script in ~1h. Thanks! :thumbsup:
